recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current source satisfies FHIR-12460 as refined by later Timing decisions, and extra prose would duplicate the authoritative datatype definition without changing implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-12460 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for the Timing datatype. It requested correction of Timing examples, Timing.repeat.when cardinality 0..*, removal of tim-3, loosening of tim-10 to prohibit only when with timeOfDay, removal of tim-11, and a note warning about incoherent combinations such as every 3 days on Friday.
initial_application: Historical commit aedd18d2bf63c6b72d72dca8285dd9fdbd904a4d, '#12460 relax constraints on Timing datatype', matches Jira's svn revision 11172 comment and changed source/datatypes.html plus Timing datatype spreadsheet/XML inputs to implement the issue.
additional_context: Timing remains an active normative datatype in source/fhir.ini and is published on datatypes.html. FHIR-12201 and FHIR-12352 introduced dayOfWeek and timeOfDay, while later Published issues FHIR-23710 and FHIR-25289 clarified that frequency and period may be combined with dayOfWeek/timeOfDay and that timeOfDay is only mutually exclusive with when.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Current source/datatypes.html has the corrected Timing example rows and cautionary note, while source/datatypes/timing.xml has Timing.repeat.when at 0..*, the multi-when union comment, tim-10 as timeOfDay.empty() or when.empty(), and no remaining old tim-3 or dayOfWeek/frequency/period tim-11 constraint.

related_jiras.note: Introduced Timing.repeat.dayOfWeek, the element whose original interaction with frequency/period was relaxed by FHIR-12460; already represented on the combined branch.
Introduced Timing.repeat.timeOfDay, which is part of the same constraint family and is correctly present in current source.
MedicationRequest dosage examples exposed the validation problem that led to FHIR-12460; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published issue corrected the timeOfDay comment to reflect FHIR-12460's tim-10 relaxation; already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published issue explicitly reaffirmed that dayOfWeek/timeOfDay wording should not prohibit frequency or period; already represented on the combined branch.
